notes.3: Many candidates found this question challenging. It required candidates to know that the acceleration of free fall without air resistance is constant, and to be able to recognise a graph indicating this. Even able candidates tended to opt for A: the graph showing that acceleration increased uniformly with time.
notes.7: Many candidates failed to read this question carefully and chose option D, giving the spring’s length rather than its extension.
notes.16: Only the very strongest candidates answered this question correctly. Option C was very popular, suggesting a belief that the temperature of ice increases as it melts.
notes.20: Option A was a common choice in this question on waves, indicating a misconception that the boat would show a steady movement in the direction of motion of a wave front.
notes.21: Wave diffraction was unfamiliar to many candidates with only the strongest candidates answering correctly.
notes.23: Despite the labelled diagram, many candidates believed that violet light refracted less at face 1 and more at face 2 (Option B).
notes.28: Although a large majority knew that electrons were involved in the charging process, the direction of movement was unclear.
notes.29: Even many of the most able candidates incorrectly thought that moving the lamp to the left side of the resistor would increase the current in it.
notes.34: All options were popular in this question on the role of an earth wire, suggesting considerable uncertainty on this topic.
notes.general_comments:
Some candidates found this paper challenging. Candidates performed best on Questions 1 and 19 while
Questions 3 and 16 proved the most difficult. Candidates should be advised to read all questions and
options carefully before choosing their answer.
